content.user_title: Run a Storm Survival Roleplay Chapter
content.value_statement: Writers need a structured way to run a high-pressure survival scene without losing pacing. This skill provides staged prompts, emotional beats, and branching outcomes for Stella on Gaia.
actual_capabilities: Provides a five-stage storm survival chapter structure.
Defines Stella Chen as the viewpoint character for roleplay responses.
Offers scripted scene beats for preparation, storm impact, outage, recovery, and aftermath.
Includes player decision points about priorities, storm-eye actions, and recovery choices.
Connects the chapter to later alien encounter, signal tower, science, and ruins arcs.
limitations: It is a narrative guide, not a weather or survival safety resource.
It does not include executable code or automation tools.
It assumes an existing Gaia planet storyline and Stella character context.
Most source text is bilingual Chinese and English, which may need localization.

use_cases.title: Interactive Fiction Session
use_cases.description: Run a tense storm chapter with staged messages, player choices, and survival consequences.

use_cases.title: Science Fiction Chapter Draft
use_cases.description: Use the storm sequence to draft a chapter with danger, isolation, recovery, and a mystery reveal.

use_cases.title: NPC Response Guide
use_cases.description: Keep Stella consistent under pressure while responding to player advice during an emergency.

prompt_templates.title: Start the Warning Scene
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for the first storm warning.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to start the storm warning scene. Keep Stella calm but worried, and ask me to choose the first priority.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Player Choice
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate interaction during preparation or the storm eye.
prompt_templates.prompt: Continue the chapter after my choice. Show Stella acting on it, include a cost or benefit, and end with the next urgent decision.

prompt_templates.title: Write the Outage Sequence
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced emotional beat without direct player interaction.
prompt_templates.prompt: Write the communication outage scene from Stella’s viewpoint. Focus on fear, endurance, and her promise to reconnect.

prompt_templates.title: Branch the Aftermath
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced continuation with consequences and future hooks.
prompt_templates.prompt: Resolve the storm aftermath using my previous choices. Show resource losses, emotional recovery, and the clue about intelligent life.

output_examples.input: Start the chapter and ask what Stella should protect first.
output_examples.output: Stella reports the scanner warning, lists shelter, supplies, water, communication, and a backup plan, then asks for the top priority.

output_examples.input: The player tells Stella to stay in shelter during the storm eye.
output_examples.output: Stella rests, repairs weak points, saves battery power, and misses some outside clues but improves her chance of surviving the second wall.

output_examples.input: End with the mysterious creature clue.
output_examples.output: Stella surveys the ruined camp, finds large three-toed tracks, and discovers technology parts missing from the ship wreckage.

best_practices: Keep each response focused on one urgent beat and one clear player choice.
Track prior choices so the aftermath reflects protected supplies, shelter damage, and missed clues.
Use sensory detail and short pauses to build pressure without removing player agency.
anti_patterns: Do not present the chapter as real survival advice or weather guidance.
Do not ignore earlier player decisions when resolving damage or discoveries.
Do not skip the emotional recovery beat before moving into the mystery hook.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create an interactive science fiction storm survival chapter starring Stella Chen on Gaia.

faq.question: Does the skill run commands or scripts?
faq.answer: No. The fenced sections are narrative examples and dialogue beats, not executable commands.

faq.question: Can I use it outside the Gaia storyline?
faq.answer: Yes, but you should adapt Stella, the scanner, the alien storm, and later chapter hooks.

faq.question: What tone should responses use?
faq.answer: Use urgent, emotional, survival-focused prose with moments of fear, resolve, relief, and caution.

faq.question: How much player control does it support?
faq.answer: It supports priority choices, storm-eye choices, and consequence-based aftermath decisions.

faq.question: Is this a safety training skill?
faq.answer: No. It is fictional writing guidance and should not replace emergency preparedness information.
